frame_of_reference: scan datum frame of scratchpad/mesh_0917/phantom_family/data/p4_datum.json: +x nose, +y left, +z up, feet plane z = -153.37 mm, motor-axis diagonal 350.0 mm.
grades: high / medium-high may enter revision 1 (plan B.0). medium / low are ablation-only. Every row below states the file, page or table it comes from.

SCAN.what: owned CC-BY Phantom 4 3D scan (NeverDun, 0.4 mm), decimated to /workspace/sionna/outputs/phantom4_scan_decim.ply, aligned by scripts/datum.py so its motor-axis diagonal is the published 350 mm and its lowest foot point is our lowest gear point
SCAN.residual: motor-axis fit residual 0.76-0.84 mm on the four rotors; datum scale 0.98686
SCAN.state_of_the_aircraft: propellers off, gimbal and camera removed (no scan point sits below z = -70 mm inside r < 60 mm), battery installed

QSG_P7.what: dimension figure: 289.5 mm x 289.5 mm footprint and 196 mm height. The 196 mm dimension line ends on the top of a propeller hub cap, so it is a props-INCLUDED height.

UM_P8.what: Aircraft Diagram: four orthographic elevations (front, rear, left side, bottom) with callouts [1] GPS ... [12] Vision Positioning Sensors
UM_P8.scale_rule: front elevation: crown row 706, feet row 1198 at 600 dpi -> 492 px for the scan's 180.21 mm -> 2.7301 px/mm. Side elevation: crown row 1924, feet row 2428 -> 504 px -> 2.7967 px/mm. Cross-check: the side elevation's two motor cans are 687.5 px apart = 245.8 mm against the geometric 247.49 mm (-0.7 %), and the front elevation's props-included height reads 195.6 mm against the QSG's 196 mm (-0.2 %). Quoted accuracy of anything read off these drawings: +-1 %.

UM_P20_21.what: Obstacle and Vision Positioning System: forward obstacle sensing plus a downward system of two ultrasonic and four monocular sensors; p.21 states the obstacle-sensing cameras are installed on the landing gear. No rear vision and no infrared side sensors are described anywhere in this manual.

SPIN.what: rotor spin: front-left and rear-right clockwise seen from above; from the User Manual v1.2 p.7 propeller figure (black ring on FL with a CCW lock arrow, silver on FR with CW) and p.23's ring-colour rule

targets.source: SCAN radial profile: r50 = 18.7-19.3 mm over z = -11 ... -1
targets.reviewer_note: RESIDUAL. This row's own target (38.6) and the frozen threshold (38.0) disagree, and the built pod measures 35.03 mm on the same r50 rule at z = -5 mm, so it passes the frozen threshold by 0.03 mm and would fail this row's 38.6 +- 3. Cause: drone_parts_rev1.motor_can tapers the pod linearly (pod_taper 0.83, widest at its bottom z = -11), while the scan's r50 is barrel-shaped: 17.8 at z = -11.1, 19.0 at -9.1, 19.3 at -5.1, 16.0 at -1.1. A single linear taper cannot reproduce that, so the pod is ~3.2 mm narrow where both are measured. Not changed by the reviewer: fixing it is a geometry change and the fingerprint is not frozen yet — it is open question Q7.

unsourced_engine_knobs.revision_1_value_mm: revision 0's 101.6 x 107.3 x 42.2 multiplied by the largest scale in drone_rev1_phantom4.INTERNAL_SCALES that fits the revision-1 shell with 1 mm of clearance
unsourced_engine_knobs.why: DJI publishes no dimension for the PH4-5350 mAh pack. The Quick Start Guide's only dimensioned figure on that page (182/172/105/71 mm) belongs to the remote controller, not the battery. The owned scan is an outside surface, so it cannot measure a pack inside the shell. Revision 0's numbers were ratio placeholders (body length x 0.50 etc.) and were not measured either.
unsourced_engine_knobs.declared: This is an engine knob, not a measurement. It must never be reported as measured. It is carried into revision 1 only because plan C.2 requires the internal metal to be inside the shell, and revision 0's box does not fit the (correctly smaller) revision-1 shell.

unsourced_engine_knobs.what: vision-sensor cylinder sizes (r 6 x 8 mm forward, r 5 x 6 mm downward)
unsourced_engine_knobs.why: DJI publishes none; these are revision 0's repo literals, carried over unchanged. Only the sensors DJI never fitted were removed.

unsourced_engine_knobs.what: superellipse exponents of the fairing sections (pod 2.6 / 2.4, arms 3.0 / 3.0) and the pod half-width profile away from x = 0
unsourced_engine_knobs.why: The scan gives section extents, not section shape. The exponents and the half-width profile are the loft's free parameters; they are chosen so the union reproduces the measured section widths at x = 0, +-30, +-60, +-90 and the measured top silhouette area, all of which are scored in C.3 and C.4.

unsourced_engine_knobs.what: downward vision pair xy on the belly (x 12.0, y +-20.0 mm)
unsourced_engine_knobs.why: Read off the p.8 bottom elevation by eye; the drawing gives no dimension and the scan cannot see the belly lenses. Their z is not chosen at all - it is set by the fairing's own belly under that xy, so the part always meets the shell.
unsourced_engine_knobs.declared: Engine knob, not a measurement. Moved here by the reviewer 2026-09-17.

review_fix_2026_09_18.what: Geometry fixes for the defects the 2026-09-17 adversarial review left standing: the motor pod (R8), the tail (R9), the arm underside (R10) and the four floating vision sensors (R11). Every number below was re-measured from the scan before the change.

new_targets.name: motor pod diameter, scan r50 rule at z = -5 mm
new_targets.measured: r50 of the scan samples within 35 mm of each rotor axis, z slab +-1.0 mm, mean over the four rotors = 18.91 mm radius. This is the same rule benchmark/mesh_rev1_acceptance.py scores and the same one the frozen threshold names (38.0 +- 3.0).
new_targets.caveat: r50 is a MEDIAN OVER A MIXTURE: the slab holds pod wall and arm fairing both. It is used because it is the rule the frozen row names, and because on this geometry the pod wall is what the median lands on (the delivery's cone wall was 17.51 mm at z = -5 and the same measurement returned 17.5). It is not the pod's true radius.
new_targets.source: SCAN raw: p4_datum_scan_samples.npy, 2e6 surface samples in the datum frame; re-measured 2026-09-18 by impl/phantom4/fixwork/{measure_targets,tailw,keel,sections}.py, ledgers fixwork/scan_targets.json and fixwork/scan_keel.json

declared_shortfalls.what: the arm keel stops at r = 144 mm; the scan's fades out at r ~ 155 (depth 1.31 mm at r = 156)
declared_shortfalls.why: carrying it further put its tip 23 mm from the rotor axis, where rib, arm tip dome and motor pod all meet, and that corner cost 60 C.1 sliver faces for the last 2 mm of rib depth. Stated rather than built.

declared_shortfalls.what: the forward vision sensor's cut against its strut is tangential on one side, so about 1.4 mm of its rim ends beside the strut rather than on it
declared_shortfalls.why: the sensor is 12 mm across and the strut it sits on is about 14 mm, with the sensor's sourced y = +-66.0 about 1.7 mm off the strut axis. Both the sensor diameter (already an unsourced engine knob) and y = +-66.0 are the delivery's; moving or shrinking the sensor to remove the tangency would be changing a knob to flatter a metric.

declared_shortfalls.what: arm stations at r <= 110 and at r = 160 keep the delivery's z_bot
declared_shortfalls.why: at r <= 110 the scan's section is a smooth U with no shoulder, and between r = 75 and 105 the landing gear sits on the arm axis so the underside is unread. r = 160 is inside the motor pod's footprint (the pod spans r = 155.7 ... 194.3 about the rotor axis), so the scan there is a mixture of pod and arm.

free_parameters_changed.why: the scan cannot separate the tail from the arm fairings inboard of x ~ -70, so this stays the loft's free parameter; it is carried linearly from the measured 38.0 at x = -70 to the delivered 40.0 at x = -50. The delivery's 32.0 left a notch between tail and arms that the scan does not have.

free_parameters_changed.what: keel loft top z (about 2 mm above the local flank) and superellipse exponents 2.4/2.4
free_parameters_changed.why: the rib has to overlap the arm fairing or the P2 union leaves a tangent seam instead of one solid. The scan gives the rib's depth and width, not its section shape.
